nodes.summary: Isomorphic trees have the same clusters.
nodes.title: Isomorphic trees have the same clusters

nodes.summary: The clusters of all vertices seen from the leaf labeled `a`. (The cluster of the leaf `a` itself is the set of all other taxa, which is also the cluster of its neighbor.)
nodes.title: Cluster set of a tree seen from a leaf

nodes.summary: The cluster of a vertex `v` seen from the leaf labeled `a`: the taxa `x ≠ a` whose leaf lies beyond `v`, i.e. `v` is on the path from the leaf `a` to the leaf `x`.
nodes.title: Cluster of a vertex seen from a leaf

nodes.summary: Every binary hierarchy on the taxa other than `a` is the cluster set, seen from the leaf `a`, of some unrooted binary phylogenetic tree (vertices: the leaf `a` and the members of the hierarchy; each member is joined to the smallest member strictly containing it).
nodes.title: Every binary hierarchy is a cluster set of a tree

nodes.summary: The clusters of a tree seen from a leaf form a binary hierarchy on the other taxa (Semple & Steel 2003, Section 3.1).
nodes.title: Clusters of an unrooted tree form a binary hierarchy

nodes.summary: The members of a binary hierarchy below a member form a binary hierarchy.
nodes.title: Binary hierarchy restricted below a member is a binary hierarchy

nodes.summary: A binary hierarchy on a finite set `S`: a family of nonempty subsets of `S` containing `S` and every singleton, any two members nested or disjoint, and every member with at least two elements the disjoint union of two members. These are the cluster systems of the rooted binary phylogenetic trees on `S` (Semple & Steel 2003, Section 3.1).
nodes.title: Binary hierarchy on a finite set

nodes.summary: Two trees with the same clusters seen from the leaf `a` are isomorphic: the clusters determine the tree.
nodes.title: Clusters determine an unrooted binary tree

nodes.summary: Two unrooted binary phylogenetic trees are isomorphic when some graph isomorphism maps the leaf with each label to the leaf with the same label.
nodes.title: Isomorphism of unrooted binary phylogenetic trees

nodes.summary: Every planar tree has at least one leaf.
nodes.title: Every planar binary tree has a leaf

nodes.summary: The multiset of leaf labels.
nodes.title: Leaf labels of a planar binary tree

nodes.summary: On a nonempty finite set `S` there are `(2 |S| - 3)‼` binary hierarchies, as many as rooted binary phylogenetic trees on `S`: a tree corresponds to the leaf sets of its subtrees.
nodes.title: The number of binary hierarchies

nodes.summary: On `n ≥ 1` labeled taxa there are `(2 n - 3)‼ = 1 · 3 · 5 ⋯ (2 n - 3)` rooted binary phylogenetic trees (`1` tree for `n = 1` and `n = 2`, `3` for `n = 3`, `15` for `n = 4`). For `n = 1` the natural-number subtraction gives `2 - 3 = 0` and `0‼ = 1`, the conventional value `(-1)‼ = 1` of the formula; the empty set of taxa (excluded here) has no tree (`isEmpty_rootedBinaryTree_empty`).
nodes.title: Schröder's count of rooted binary phylogenetic trees

nodes.summary: The count `(2 n - 5)‼` of unrooted binary phylogenetic trees holds from `n = 2` taxa on: for `n = 2` the single tree is one edge and `2 · 2 - 5 = 0` in `ℕ`, `0‼ = 1` (the conventional value `(-1)‼ = 1`). For `n ≤ 1` there is no tree while the formula gives `1`.
nodes.title: Number of unrooted binary phylogenetic trees

nodes.summary: On `n ≥ 3` labeled taxa there are `(2 n - 5)‼ = 1 · 3 ⋯ (2 n - 5)` unrooted binary phylogenetic trees up to label-preserving isomorphism.
nodes.title: The number of unrooted binary phylogenetic trees

nodes.summary: The planar drawings of rooted binary trees on the taxa `X`: planar trees whose leaves are labeled by `X`, each taxon labeling exactly one leaf.
nodes.title: Planar drawings of rooted binary trees on a taxon set

nodes.summary: A planar rooted binary tree with leaves labeled by `α`: a leaf `leaf a`, or an internal vertex `node l r` with left subtree `l` and right subtree `r` (the children are ordered).
nodes.title: Planar rooted binary tree with labeled leaves

nodes.summary: Unrooted binary phylogenetic trees up to label-preserving isomorphism correspond to the binary hierarchies on the taxa other than `a`, by their clusters seen from the leaf `a`.
nodes.title: Unrooted binary trees correspond to binary hierarchies

nodes.summary: The rooted binary phylogenetic trees on the taxa `X`: planar drawings with leaf set `X` modulo exchanging the two children of internal vertices, i.e. rooted binary trees with unordered children and leaves labeled bijectively by `X`, up to label-preserving isomorphism.
nodes.title: Rooted binary phylogenetic tree

nodes.summary: One swap: exchange the two children of one internal vertex (anywhere in the tree).
nodes.title: Swap of the children of an internal vertex

nodes.summary: An unrooted binary phylogenetic tree on the taxa `X`: a finite tree `G` on a vertex type `V` whose degree-one vertices are labeled bijectively by `X` (`label`) and whose other vertices all have degree three.
nodes.title: Unrooted binary phylogenetic tree

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
